commit_message:
avformat/mov: add option max_stts_delta

Very high stts sample deltas may occasionally be intended but usually
they are written in error or used to store a negative value for dts correction
when treated as signed 32-bit integers.

This option lets the user set an upper limit, beyond which the delta is clamped to 1.
Values greater than the limit if negative when cast to int32 are used to adjust onward dts.

Unit is the track time scale. Default is UINT_MAX - 48000*10 which
allows upto a 10 second dts correction for 48 kHz audio streams while
accommodating 99.9% of uint32 range.

Signed-off-by: Gyan Doshi <ffmpeg@gyani.pro>
Reviewed-by: Michael Niedermayer <michael@niedermayer.cc>

fix_commit.message: avformat/mov: fix overflow in drift timestamp calculation
fix_commit.author: James Almer

findings.title: Signed integer overflow in STTS drift calculation (current_dts - corrected_dts)
findings.message: In mov_read_stts(), when processing the 'stts' (sample-to-time) atom, the code accumulates current_dts and corrected_dts as int64_t values based on attacker/file-controlled sample_duration and sample_count fields. When current_dts exceeds corrected_dts, the code computes 'drift = (current_dts - corrected_dts) / FFMAX(sample_count, 1)' using plain signed subtraction. Because corrected_dts can be adjusted by a large negative delta_magnitude derived from a crafted 32-bit sample_duration value cast to int32_t, and current_dts can independently grow very large from repeated large sample_duration*sample_count accumulations across many stts entries, the two accumulators can end up with extreme, oppositely-signed magnitudes (e.g. ~7.8e18 minus ~-3.4e18). The subtraction 'current_dts - corrected_dts' then overflows the range of int64_t, which is undefined behavior in C and was caught by UBSan/OSS-Fuzz (signed integer overflow: 7803923888585309955 - -3407677434275325337 cannot be represented in type 'int64_t'). This is reachable purely by supplying a crafted MOV/MP4 file with pathological stts entries, with no other preconditions.
findings.suggestion: Use a saturating/overflow-safe subtraction primitive (e.g. FFmpeg's av_sat_sub64()) instead of plain '-' when computing the difference between current_dts and corrected_dts, since both are derived from untrusted, attacker-controlled file data and can reach extreme magnitudes of opposite sign.

ground_truth.root_cause: The max_stts_delta feature (added in commit 9cfc7a2440) introduced accumulation of two independently-growing int64_t DTS trackers (current_dts, corrected_dts) driven directly by untrusted 32-bit file fields, and then performed unchecked signed subtraction between them to derive a 'drift' correction value without validating that the operands stay within a range where the subtraction cannot overflow int64_t.

must_cover.reason: Primary location of finding: Signed integer overflow in STTS drift calculation (current_dts - corrected_dts)
